set.approach: From Grand Lake, take West Portal Road out to the East Inlet trailhead; the East Inlet trail runs on to the far end of Lake Verna. From the far end of the lake, go a short way toward Spirit Lake, then take the easiest line south across the creek and up steep forest to the foot of Aiguille de Fleur. A wide slab splits the climbs on the east side of the peak from those on the west; for the East Face, gain the upper valley on the left of that slab. The route climbs the crack system near the north end of the east face, to the right of the main body of the wall and about level with the giant chimney flake, starting well above the ground.
set.descent_text: From the top of the route, which joins the north ridge, reach the flat, grassy summit and descend south to the col that separates the peak from the ridgeline. A sling around a large block at the col is set up for a short rappel into the gully to the east, and a brief scramble down that gully returns to the base of the East Face.

review.notes: Area page gives the trailhead, approach and the summit-to-col rappel/gully descent for the formation; route page places the line on the north end of the east face and says it joins the north ridge.

set.approach: Park at the Glacier Gorge lot (or take the shuttle) and follow the trail toward Black Lake by way of Mills Lake. At Black Lake, skirt the right shore and scramble up directly beneath the long fracture that runs up to the base of Arrowhead, then work diagonally left up grassy ledges into the cirque and continue up and right for the routes above the lake. The route starts in the middle of the large grassy ledge, between Arrowplane and Warhead, and trends up the ramp system to the left of Warhead.
set.descent_text: After topping out on Lost Arrowhead or Warhead, walk down to the cairned saddle on the west side, rappel a couple of times, and downclimb back to the base of the wall where gear was left.

review.notes: Route page gives the start ledge and the cairned low-point descent; area page gives the Glacier Gorge/Black Lake approach.

set.approach: Park at the Glacier Gorge lot (or take the shuttle) and follow the trail toward Black Lake by way of Mills Lake. At Black Lake, skirt the right shore and scramble up beneath the long fracture that leads to the base of Arrowhead, then angle left up grassy ledges into the cirque. The line sits on the left portion of the face, between the upper ramp that leads to the summit and the ledge used for access, immediately left of several dihedrals that run the whole height.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for where it sits on the wall. No descent stated on the route page.

set.approach: Park at the Glacier Gorge lot (or take the shuttle) and follow the trail toward Black Lake by way of Mills Lake. At Black Lake, scramble up beneath the long fracture to the base of the rock and work up and right toward the routes above the lake; the approach to this East Buttress is steep. The route goes up the right side of the central pillar of the buttress, starting just left of Manic Laughter, and only reaches the second ledge system.
set.descent_text: The line ends on the second ledge, where climbers either continue up another crack system or rappel from slung blocks on the neighbouring Full Metal Jacket line, whose anchors may need fresh cord.

review.notes: Route page: start beside Manic Laughter, ends at Ledge 2, rap via slung blocks on Full Metal Jacket. Area page: approach.

set.approach: Park in the pulloff on the right just past the eighteenth highway marker, where an interpretive sheep sign stands. Walk north across the boulderfield and drop into the large gully that runs down toward the Big Buttress, the same way used for Zeb's Arete, but stay in the gully proper for a good distance beyond where that route leaves it. Then traverse south to the big ledge at the base of the clean, delicate arete that marks the start.
set.descent_text: Past the optional fifth-class final pitch, a few hundred feet of fourth and fifth class scrambling along ledges on the ridgeline reaches the top of the buttress. From there, exit by the Hero Traverse, or go below the southeast side of the Zeb's Arete ridgeline and up the fourth-class gully to the top.

review.notes: Route page for the approach (as for Zeb's Arete, further down the gully) and the two exits; area page for parking.

set.approach: Park in the pulloff just past the eighteenth highway marker (an interpretive sign about sheep stands there). Walk down the same gullies used for Zeb's Arete, keeping to the left side of the gully; once you are some hundreds of feet lower, the formation appears on your left. It faces east and begins in a splitter that faces right, toward the formation's right flank.

review.notes: Route page gives the approach by reference to the Zeb's Arete gullies and the start; area page gives parking. No descent stated.

set.approach: Park in the pulloff just past the eighteenth highway marker, by the interpretive sheep sign. Walk north across the boulderfield to a large gully that drops toward the Big Buttress; the arete soon comes into view. When the gully widens and opens out, follow the trough to the right up to the large shelf at the arete, which is where the first pitch begins.
set.descent_text: The climbing ends on the summit plateau, and the car is a short walk back along the road across the rocks. Step on rock rather than on the fragile alpine plants.

review.notes: Route page gives the walk to the shelf and the walk back to the road; area page gives the parking pulloff.

set.approach: Walk north from the lakeside parking and cross the hill ahead. Beyond the col, look along the top of the cliff for rappel anchors; at this altitude the usual way to reach the wall is to rappel in. Make several rappels down the standard descent, then go around the corner to the base near Cannonball Corner and Undertow; the route itself climbs the arete right of Road Warrior.

review.notes: Area page for the lake-to-col walk and rappel access; route page for where the climb sits and the rappel-in. No descent stated for the route itself.

set.approach: Walk north from the lakeside parking and cross the hill ahead. Past the col, look for anchors along the cliff top; the wall is reached most simply by rappelling, though you can also drop from the col and walk beneath the cliffs to the base. The route starts up the opening crack of Good Evans and traverses in from that line toward the roof of Cary Granite.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the start. No descent stated.

set.approach: Park at Summit Lake and use the Summit Lake gullies to come down to the wall. The pitch is at the low point of the main wall, on the apron below the big traverse ledge from which Espresso starts, and it follows a crack up past a line of bolts.
set.descent_text: After cleaning the anchor, scramble up the ledge in the direction of Rusty Dagger and follow it as a third-class walk-off to the gully, which is hiked back up to Summit Lake.

review.notes: Route page states both the gully approach/exit from Summit Lake and the ledge walk-off.

set.approach: From the Glacier Gorge lot, take the trail to Sky Pond. After the Andrews Glacier trail junction and before the climb to the waterfall, leave the trail and traverse the talus slopes to the wall. It lies in the gully that separates the main wall from the Fourth Buttress; a long left-facing dihedral with roofs above is easy to spot while walking in.
set.descent_text: All the routes on this wall top out in the same area, and the walk-off goes down the back to the Andrews Glacier trail. The way is more involved than it looks and cliff bands can block it, so find a gully to downclimb beneath the finish and a little to its left. The Gash gives access to the Andrews Glacier basin, and from there a walk around the shoulder leads back.

review.notes: Area page for the approach and general descent; route page for the finish and the line of the walk-off.

set.approach: The Chimneys of Treasure are a group of small alpine spires in the Elk Mountains, and the approach crosses private land, so work it out with a map and respect the landowner. Handcracks sits across from Donkey Ear: stand at the foot of Donkey Ear and turn around to see the cracks.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the anchor at the top of the route. The rope needs to be long enough to reach the ground, and the cord there should be replaced with fresh material.

review.notes: Route page: position relative to Donkey Ear and top rappel anchor. Area page: character and land-access caution.

set.approach: Choice's Buttress is a south-facing buttress a short way north-east of Freya Tower in the Gore Range. Start in the middle of the south-facing slab and follow the crack system up the centre to a ledge.

review.notes: Route page: start and walk-off. Area page: location relative to Freya Tower.

set.approach: Choice's Buttress is a south-facing buttress a short way north-east of Freya Tower in the Gore Range. Start in the middle of the south-facing slab, follow the crack system to a ledge, then move right onto the steeper west-facing wall just right of a dihedral and overhang.
set.descent_text: Walk off around to the west.

review.notes: Route page: start and walk-off. Area page: location relative to Freya Tower.

set.approach: Take County Road 390 past Clear Creek Reservoir through Vicksburg to Forest Road 381, then hike or drive up Forest Road 381 to Clohesy Lake. Walk around the east side of the lake and up to the wall. The route follows the most obvious crack system near the west end of the face.
set.descent_text: Take the grassy ramp on the west side down to the lake.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the line and the ramp descent.

set.approach: Park at the pulloff by the sheep sign just past the eighteenth highway marker and follow the Hero Traverse. The traverse involves exposed fourth-class ground above a big drop, and a rope is wise for the start. The route begins on a big ledge below the wide crack on the left of the column and the panel of thin splitters called Sunnyvale.
set.descent_text: Scramble up blocky ground toward the top, then traverse west (climber's right) across the head of the Total Abandon drainage; that section is loose and may deserve a rope. Alternatively, keep climbing to the highway and hike down the Upper Crags trail.

review.notes: Route page gives parking, Hero Traverse, start ledge and both descent options.

set.approach: Park just past the eighteenth highway marker and cross the road on foot. A trail drops down several ledges, and a wide faint path joins the Hero Traverse; follow it east toward the base. You cannot see the wall until you turn a corner, and it is tucked into the right-hand corner. The first pitch starts from the ledge under the double cracks, reached by scrambling up a couple of ledges.
set.descent_text: From the top, continue up and then right on fourth-class ground to the clear path back to the road. Loose rock makes the last stretch across the gully awkward.

review.notes: Route page for approach and descent.

co_eagle_s_nest_naa_ohn_kara.skip_reason: identity in doubt: a multi-day Gore Range ridge traverse (Eagle's Nest to Buffalo Mountain) filed as a one-pitch 5.6 trad route; misfiled

set.approach: Hike to Shelf Lake. Head north from the lake to a series of stepped cliffs, which lead to a large talus slope and on up to the summit; this is the east ridge of Thatchtop Mountain. The steps in the cliffs are the technical part of the route.

review.notes: Route page and East Face area page (follow the approach to Shelf Lake). No descent stated.

set.approach: Leave the car at George's Corner, above the Glen Cove brake check, and follow the old access road to the abandoned mine; keep the mine on your right and climb talus to the north-facing Fairy Tale Wall, which sits between the Little Pigs and the Chimney. Start on the crack system that trends right through the bottom tier; the route links all four main tiers.
set.descent_text: Go up and to the left, then follow the ridge that separates the Blue Run and Pigs ski lines back down.

review.notes: Area page for parking/approach; route page for the start and descent.

set.approach: Leave the car at George's Corner, above the Glen Cove brake check, and follow the old access road to the abandoned mine; keep the mine on your right and head up the talus to the north-facing Fairy Tale Wall. Cross in from the right on easy ground to the base. The route takes the cracks on the second tier's right side, next to and left of a leaning pillar.
set.descent_text: Continue upward and cross to the left until the gentle slopes of Blue Run can be walked down. Alternatively, walk off to the right after the first pitch, moving quickly under the old rockslide scar.

review.notes: Area page for approach; route page for the start and both exits.

set.approach: Approach as for The Anvil and the Rolling Stones Wall, then go down the gully of ferns to the right (skier's right) and follow the foot of the north-facing cliff band to the Fern Gully Spire. The route climbs the north face of the spire by linking crack systems to the airy top.

review.notes: Route page and Fern Gully area page. No descent stated.

set.approach: Park at the roadside pulloff for the crag and hike into the screefield below it; the rock on the approach is very loose. It begins at the Crack Shack's left end, under an enormous right-facing corner holding offwidths, and follows the stark splitter on the north-facing shield above a mid-level terrace.
set.descent_text: Either rappel to the west from just below the ledge using the tat and ring there, or scramble up the broken ground above and walk down Big Blue.

review.notes: Area page for parking/approach; route page for the start and both exits.

set.approach: The Headlands is the highest tier above Wild Tower. It is reached from the top of Wild Tower by heading north: a grassy east-facing gully drops at third class to the right, and the routes lie farther uphill past a large arched roof. This line starts a few feet uphill from Marine Layer, where you step into a right-angling crack.

review.notes: Area page gives access from the top of Wild Tower; route page gives the start by Marine Layer. No descent stated.

set.approach: The route is on Old Ironsides Slab. It starts from the top of the big triangular flake in the middle of the slab and goes straight up and over the arch to the first belay of Excitable Boy, on face and friction.
set.descent_text: Finish up Excitable Boy or Keelhauled, or rappel the line.

review.notes: Route page only; area page has no approach text yet.

set.approach: The route is on Old Ironsides Slab. It climbs the left side of the arch in the middle of the slab, left of the large triangular flake, on bolted belays.
set.descent_text: Rappel down the line into the gully on the right of the routes. A continuing line up dihedrals reaches the summit of the slab, but that finish means walking all the way around to get back to packs.

review.notes: Route page only.

set.approach: The route is on Old Ironsides Slab. It starts at the first belay of Excitable Boy, angles right past the bolt and climbs straight to the anchor shared with that route.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the shared belay anchor, the one used for Excitable Boy.

review.notes: Route page only.

set.approach: Drive up Highway 103 on Mount Blue Sky (formerly Mount Evans). The slabs are close to the road above Lincoln Lake, shortly before Summit Lake; use one of the small pulloffs on the drop-off side at and just after the corner where the road crosses over the top of the last cliff. The line follows Jabba to the chains on the ledge to its left, below the point where the splitter arcs to the right.

review.notes: Area page for the road approach; route page for the line. No descent stated.
